papers.title_en: Enhancing Transformer Representations of Symbolic ODE Expressions
papers.authors: Xiyue Fan, Adam Prugel-Bennett, Stuart E. Middleton
papers.evidence: 面向符号表达式与符号回归的Transformer表示
papers.tldr: 符号常微分方程求解多依赖数值近似或盲搜索，缺乏保持交换律的结构化表示。核心方法：在Transformer中引入树位置编码，并基于学到的结构表示用对比学习支持数学交换律。关键结果：树位置编码在训练早期即加速学习，并随训练持续提升，在不同数据规模和任务上均获一致优势。贡献意义：为符号数学表达式的结构化建模与推理提供了有效方案，并通过消融揭示方法间交互。
papers.abstract_en: Existing approaches to solving differential equations, such as symbolic regression, physics informed neural networks, and neural operators, typically focus on numerical approximations or blind symbolic search via fitting to numerical data. Less attention has been paid to learning structured representations of mathematical expressions that preserve commutative properties and could support mathematical reasoning in symbolic forms. Transformer models have shown strong capabilities in solving symbolic differential equations. However, standard positional embeddings in transformers are designed for sequence data. Symbolic differential equations are naturally represented by expression trees, so these positional embeddings may not efficiently capture their hierarchical structures. We investigate existing tree positional embeddings in symbolic ordinary differential equation (ODE) tasks. We systematically study their effectiveness under different settings. Our results show that tree positional embeddings aid learning in early epochs and continue to improve performance throughout, ultimately yielding consistent advantages across various data sizes and tasks. Based on learned structural representations, we apply contrastive learning to support the commutative property in mathematics. Ablation studies provide insight into how these methods interact in modelling symbolic mathematical structures.

papers.title_en: An Efficient Symbolic Algorithm for Computing Lyapunov Constants in Planar Switching Systems
papers.authors: Cheng Zheng, Laigang Guo, Xiangyu Wang
papers.evidence: 用符号代数算法计算切换系统的李雅普诺夫常数，属传统稳定性分析
papers.tldr: 平面切换系统的 Lyapunov 常数对分岔分析至关重要，但经典 Poincaré 映射需反复符号积分，高阶计算困难。本文把向量场映射到复域，基于 Laurent 多项式构造法式算法，用直接代数运算替代连续积分。对广义切换四次 Liénard 系统，算法给出中心条件并证明存在 10 个小幅极限环，刷新循环数下界；对 Alpazur 振荡器电路修正模型，证明至多一个且可达。该框架高效支持实际分段光滑系统的复杂动力学分析。
papers.abstract_en: Lyapunov constants are a crucial tool for analyzing bifurcation behavior in switching systems. This paper proposes an efficient algebraic symbolic algorithm for computing Lyapunov constants in planar switching systems. By mapping the vector fields into the complex domain, we construct a normal form algorithm based on Laurent poly?nomials. The classical Poincaré map method requires repeated symbolic integration, which may lead to substantial computational difficulties at high orders. Our ap?proach improves computational efficiency by replacing continuous integration with direct algebraic operations. We apply this approach to investigate two switching models. For a generalized switching quartic Liénard system, the algebraic method extracts the center conditions and proves the existence of 10 small-amplitude limit cycles, establishing a new lower bound for its cyclicity. Furthermore, a physically motivated circuit-level modification of the Alpazur oscillator is investigated. We show that at most one small-amplitude limit cycle can bifurcate from the center and that this upper bound is attainable, illustrating the applicability of the proposed algorithm to a practical switching circuit. This application shows that our method provides a systematic framework for analyzing and interpreting complex dynamical phenomena arising in practical piecewise smooth systems.

papers.title_en: Scalable Incremental Robustness Analysis of Neural Network Feedback Systems
papers.authors: Zichen Wang, Peter Seiler, Geir Dullerud, Bin Hu
papers.evidence: 为神经网络反馈系统提供可扩展的增量稳定性与性能证书
papers.tldr: 针对含深度神经网络的反馈系统，传统SDP证书随神经元总数增长而难以扩展，小增益测试虽可扩展却偏保守。本文提出统一可扩展的增量鲁棒稳定性与性能分析框架，将全阶SDP条件结构化分解，并结合可扩展Lipschitz常数估计算法，得到降维验证条件。所得LMI维度仅依赖网络最后两层宽度，与网络深度无关，并保留对象与NN耦合，小增益条件为特例。多轮交替更新进一步降低保守性，数值实验在大规模NN反馈系统上取得最优增量ℓ2增益界。
papers.abstract_en: Semidefinite programming (SDP) certificates for feedback systems containing deep neural networks (NNs) typically scale with the total number of neurons, whereas small-gain tests are scalable but can be highly conservative. This paper develops a unified and scalable framework for incremental robust stability and performance analysis of feedback interconnections involving high-dimensional NNs and unmodeled dynamics. By combining a structured decomposition of the full-order SDP condition with scalable Lipschitz constant estimation algorithms, we derive reduced verification conditions that certify incremental convergence and incremental $\ell_2$-gain bounds. The dimensions of the resulting control-analysis linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) depend only on the widths of the last two network layers and are \textit{independent of network depth}. The framework preserves the coupling between the plant and the NN, with the incremental small-gain condition recovered as a special case. To further reduce conservatism, we develop a multi-round alternating update scheme that iteratively refines the coupling variables while preserving scalability. Numerical experiments show that the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art incremental $\ell_2$-gain bounds for large-scale NN feedback systems.
